raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`QwenSparseAttnBackend._graph_speculative_layout` builds the per-row metadata for
every speculative graph replay (target-verify and draft-extend), so it runs on the
decode critical path. It expands `req_pool_indices` into one entry per row:

```python
repeats = extend_lengths.to(device=req_pool_indices.device, dtype=torch.long)
row_req_pool_indices = torch.repeat_interleave(req_pool_indices[:bs], repeats)
```

`repeats` is a device tensor, so without `output_size` the op has to know
`sum(repeats)` on the host to allocate the result: it reads the sum back from the
device, which is a host sync. The sum is already on the host a few lines above as
`actual_rows = row_lengths.numel()`, because `row_lengths` is assembled as one run
per `extend_lengths` entry.

Same pattern as #45275, which added `output_size=` to the `repeat_interleave` in
`deepseek_v4_backend.py` for the same reason.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/qwen_sparse_attn_backend.py`: pass
  `output_size=actual_rows` to `torch.repeat_interleave`, with a comment stating
  why that value is the sum.
- New `test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_qsa_graph_speculative_layout.py`
  (registered CPU unit test, no server, no weights). It pins the identity the
  argument depends on — one row per token slot, one run per extend length, in
  row-major order — over uniform extends, ragged extends, zero-length extends,
  `extend > seq_len` (the `clamp_max` path), padded rows, tail padding up to the
  captured capacity, and the capacity-overflow `ValueError`.

## Accuracy Tests

The change is behaviour-preserving; `output_size` only pre-declares the size that
the op would otherwise compute by reading the device.

- The new unit test passes unchanged against both the pre-change and post-change
  source (8/8 both ways), i.e. it asserts outputs that the patch does not alter.
- Separately, an 84-case grid (bs 1/2/4/8/16/24/32 x target-verify and
  draft-extend x uniform/ragged/zero extends x `num_padding` 0/1/bs x spare
  capacity) compared the three returned tensors with and without `output_size`:
  identical shape, dtype and values in all cases.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Isolated measurement of just this call. Ascend 910 (`torch 2.10.0`,
`torch_npu 2.10.0`), `repeats` on device, median host wall time per call over 40
iterations:

| batch | queue state | without `output_size` | with `output_size` |
| ----: | ----------- | --------------------: | -----------------: |
| 1 | idle | 75.8 us | 19.1 us |
| 32 | idle | 79.2 us | 19.3 us |
| 1 | deep (40 x 4096^3 matmuls in flight) | 65,099 us | 37.0 us |
| 32 | deep | 65,220 us | 42.0 us |

The deep-queue numbers are the queued device work being drained by the sync, not
time saved per step; they are there to show that the call is a sync point rather
than to claim 65 ms. On an idle queue the call itself is ~4x cheaper (-60 us).

End-to-end, this change on its own is inside run-to-run noise, which is what one
removed sync per step should look like: on the same machine with a Qwen3-Next-style
hybrid model (TP2, `--speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 1
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 2`, full decode graphs), decode ITL p50 moved by
-0.44 / -0.14 / +0.03 / -0.35 / -0.13 ms at batch 1 / 4 / 8 / 16 / 32, against a
same-config noise floor of 0.37 ms median and 0.91 ms max measured over 8 server
launches. I did not measure on CUDA; the mechanism (a device-side `repeats`
forcing a host read of its sum) is not platform specific.

`pre-commit run --files <the two files>`: all hooks pass.
`python3 test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_qsa_graph_speculative_layout.py`: 8 tests, OK.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (not applicable)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

+        # row_lengths is the concatenation of one run per extend_lengths entry.

         # the runner packs real rows first, so give the tail inert metadata.

@@ -0,0 +1,152 @@
+"""Unit tests for QSA's graph speculative row layout -- no server, no weights.
+
+``QwenSparseAttnBackend._graph_speculative_layout`` builds the per-row metadata
+every speculative graph replay reads. It expands ``req_pool_indices`` with
+``repeat_interleave(..., output_size=actual_rows)``, so the test pins the
+contract that makes passing ``output_size`` correct: the expansion has exactly
+``row_lengths.numel()`` entries, one run per extend length, in row-major order.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.srt.layers.attention.qwen_sparse_attn_backend import QwenSparseAttnBackend
+from sglang.srt.model_executor.forward_mode import ForwardMode
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+
+class _SpecInfo:
+    """The two attributes the layout reads off the speculative input."""
+
+    def __init__(self, draft_token_num=None, extend_seq_lens_cpu=None):
+        self.draft_token_num = draft_token_num
+        if extend_seq_lens_cpu is not None:
+            self.extend_seq_lens_cpu = extend_seq_lens_cpu
+
+
+def _expected_rows(seq_lens, extend_lens, target_verify):
+    """Reference expansion, written out per request."""
+    lengths, prefixes, requests = [], [], []
+    for i, (seq_len, extend_len) in enumerate(zip(seq_lens, extend_lens)):
+        effective = seq_len + extend_len if target_verify else seq_len
+        prefix = max(effective - extend_len, 0)
+        for k in range(extend_len):
+            lengths.append(min(prefix + 1 + k, effective))
+            prefixes.append(prefix)
+            requests.append(i)
+    return lengths, prefixes, requests
+
+
+class TestQsaGraphSpeculativeLayout(CustomTestCase):
+    def _run(self, seq_lens, extend_lens, target_verify, num_padding=0, slack=0):
+        bs = len(seq_lens)
+        kept = bs - max(0, min(num_padding, bs))
+        effective_extend = list(extend_lens[:kept]) + [0] * (bs - kept)
+        num_tokens = sum(effective_extend) + slack
+        req_pool_indices = torch.arange(bs, dtype=torch.int32)
+        if target_verify:
+            forward_mode = ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY
+            spec_info = _SpecInfo(draft_token_num=extend_lens[0])
+        else:
+            forward_mode = ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND_V2
+            spec_info = _SpecInfo(extend_seq_lens_cpu=list(extend_lens))
+        row_lengths, row_req_pool_indices, row_prefix_lengths = (
+            QwenSparseAttnBackend._graph_speculative_layout(
+                bs,
+                num_tokens,
+                req_pool_indices,
+                torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int64),
+                forward_mode,
+                spec_info,
+                num_padding=num_padding,
+            )
+        )
+        exp_lengths, exp_prefixes, exp_requests = _expected_rows(
+            seq_lens[:kept], effective_extend[:kept], target_verify
+        )
+        real = len(exp_lengths)
+        self.assertEqual(row_lengths[:real].tolist(), exp_lengths)
+        self.assertEqual(row_prefix_lengths[:real].tolist(), exp_prefixes)
+        self.assertEqual(row_req_pool_indices[:real].tolist(), exp_requests)
+        # Every output is one row per token slot, padding included; this is the
+        # identity output_size relies on.
+        for name, out in (
+            ("row_lengths", row_lengths),
+            ("row_req_pool_indices", row_req_pool_indices),
+            ("row_prefix_lengths", row_prefix_lengths),
+        ):
+            self.assertEqual(out.numel(), num_tokens, name)
+        self.assertEqual(row_lengths.dtype, torch.int32)
+        self.assertEqual(row_prefix_lengths.dtype, torch.int32)
+
+    def test_uniform_extend_draft_extend(self):
+        for bs in (1, 2, 8):
+            with self.subTest(bs=bs):
+                self._run(list(range(10, 10 + bs)), [2] * bs, target_verify=False)
+
+    def test_uniform_extend_target_verify(self):
+        for bs in (1, 4):
+            with self.subTest(bs=bs):
+                self._run([64, 65, 1023, 1024][:bs], [2] * bs, target_verify=False)
+                self._run([64, 65, 1023, 1024][:bs], [2] * bs, target_verify=True)
+
+    def test_ragged_extend(self):
+        self._run([7, 1000, 33, 2048], [1, 4, 2, 3], target_verify=False)
+
+    def test_zero_length_extends(self):
+        self._run([7, 1000, 33, 2048], [0, 4, 0, 3], target_verify=False)
+
+    def test_extend_longer_than_sequence_clamps(self):
+        # prefix is floored at 0 and each row is capped at the sequence length
+        self._run([1, 2, 3], [4, 4, 4], target_verify=False)
+
+    def test_padded_rows_are_inert(self):
+        seq_lens, extend_lens = [12, 34, 56, 78], [2, 2, 2, 2]
+        self._run(seq_lens, extend_lens, target_verify=False, num_padding=2)
+        bs = len(seq_lens)
+        req_pool_indices = torch.arange(bs, dtype=torch.int32)
+        row_lengths, row_req_pool_indices, row_prefix_lengths = (
+            QwenSparseAttnBackend._graph_speculative_layout(
+                bs,
+                4,  # capacity for the two unpadded requests
+                req_pool_indices,
+                torch.tensor(seq_lens, dtype=torch.int64),
+                ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND_V2,
+                _SpecInfo(extend_seq_lens_cpu=extend_lens),
+                num_padding=2,
+            )
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(row_req_pool_indices.tolist(), [0, 0, 1, 1])
+        self.assertEqual(row_prefix_lengths.tolist(), [10, 10, 32, 32])
+        self.assertEqual(row_lengths.tolist(), [11, 12, 33, 34])
+
+    def test_tail_padding_fills_to_capacity(self):
+        # A replay can carry fewer rows than the captured shape: the tail must be
+        # inert metadata rather than a short tensor.
+        bs = 2
+        req_pool_indices = torch.arange(bs, dtype=torch.int32)
+        row_lengths, row_req_pool_indices, row_prefix_lengths = (
+            QwenSparseAttnBackend._graph_speculative_layout(
+                bs,
+                6,  # capacity 6, only 4 real rows
+                req_pool_indices,
+                torch.tensor([12, 34], dtype=torch.int64),
+                ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND_V2,
+                _SpecInfo(extend_seq_lens_cpu=[2, 2]),
+            )
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(row_lengths.tolist(), [11, 12, 33, 34, 1, 1])
+        self.assertEqual(row_prefix_lengths.tolist(), [10, 10, 32, 32, 0, 0])
+        self.assertEqual(row_req_pool_indices.tolist(), [0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0])
+
+    def test_capacity_overflow_is_rejected(self):
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            self._run([12, 34], [4, 4], target_verify=False, slack=-4)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
